as_told.title: A chess champion's moves made themselves before a tournament, blamed on aliens

plain: The chess grandmaster Vasily Smyslov is said to have seen an alien appear before him in a German hotel room in the 1970s, while he was preparing for a match against the player Robert Hübner. Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of one of Russia's republics, tells the story in a December 2025 episode. He passes on what he heard about Smyslov and his wife, Nadezhda Smyslova, and points to Smyslov's own records of the game. According to Xenov, Smyslov was working out his moves when "an alien appeared right before him." If true, it would mean an outside intelligence stepped into a top-level chess game. Michels retells the story in a January 2026 episode with a surgeon, crediting Xenov but not naming the player. In his version, one of the greatest chess players was playing through a simulation before a big tournament, "the moves made themselves", and the player put this down to some kind of alien help. So the two tellings differ: Xenov has an alien appearing, and Michels has the moves playing on their own.
